title: High Protein Tandoori Butter Chicken Bowls
summary: Meal-prep tandoori chicken baked on a sheet pan, folded into a blended cashew-tomato butter chicken sauce, served over seasoned basmati rice with a Middle Eastern salad. Makes 10 bowls at 634 calories and 47 g protein each. The method and the timings are all on screen, but the ingredient cards give names only.

ingredients.item: Boneless chicken thighs, cut into cubes

steps.text: Cut the boneless chicken thighs into cubes.
Add the seasoning mix — salt, turmeric, tandoori masala, garam masala, paprika — with minced garlic, low-fat yogurt, a squeeze of lemon juice and olive oil.
Mix until the colour of the chicken changes.
Spread the marinated chicken evenly on a large sheet pan.
Oven bake and grill 20 minutes at 200 °C / 400 °F, then 5–7 extra minutes on grill/broil until golden brown and juicy.
On medium heat, melt the light butter with the chopped onion.
Add the seasoning — tandoori masala, parsley, cumin — with cinnamon sticks and tomato paste; mix and toast 3–4 minutes.
Add the cooked basmati rice and mix until fluffy and golden yellow.
In a large deep pan on medium heat, add light butter, sliced onion, garlic and the seasoning — garam masala, paprika, turmeric, chilli powder.
Add the cashew nuts and canned peeled tomatoes; cook 5 more minutes.
Let it cool down, then blend 2–3 minutes until completely smooth.
Return it to the pan with evaporated milk, light cream cheese and extra butter; stir until silky, rich and creamy.
Add the baked tandoori chicken to the sauce and mix until creamy and indulgent.
Put all the salad ingredients listed on screen in a large bowl.
Give it a good mix, then store in the fridge to keep fresh and crisp for the week.
Serve the fluffy rice with the creamy butter chicken, topped with yogurt; divide into 10 bowls.

nutrition.note: Number matches the end card shown on screen. The voiceover says “only 600 calories”, 34 kcal below the card and description — the spoken figure is a rounded hook.

notes: On-screen cards name the ingredients but give almost no amounts: the only quantity in the whole video is 1600 g of chicken thighs. The rest is kept for the creator's paid cookbook (link in bio, advertised at 50% off, 200+ recipes).
Voiceover says bake/grill 25 minutes; the card says 20 minutes at 200 °C / 400 °F plus 5–7 minutes grill/broil, which lands on 25–27 minutes.
The salad card also lists pomegranate, honey, sumac and chilli flakes, which the voiceover skips (“all the ingredients listed on screen”).
FeastRecipes runs the same funnel as its pesto chicken subs short: teach the method free, withhold the written quantities, sell the PDF — see the pesto-chicken-subs card for the companion capture.
gaps: No amounts for the marinade: seasoning mix (salt, turmeric, tandoori masala, garam masala, paprika), garlic, yogurt, lemon juice or olive oil.
No amounts for the rice: butter, onion, the rice seasoning, cinnamon sticks, tomato paste or basmati rice.
No amounts for the sauce: butter, onion, garlic, spices, cashews, tomatoes, evaporated milk, cream cheese.
No amounts for the salad or the yogurt topping.
Rice cooking itself (water ratio, absorption) is not covered — the video starts from “cooked basmati rice”.
No storage/reheat instructions beyond “store the salad in the fridge”.

source.quantity_basis: 1600 g chicken from the on-screen card (pixels); every other amount is unstated — the cards list ingredient names only. Macros from the end card and the video description. Times from the on-screen cook cards, cross-checked against the voiceover.
